MycoHalo: colour-calibrated quantification of fungal melanization in confrontation assays

Source: R/MycoHalo-package.R
MycoHalo-package.Rd

MycoHalo measures melanization of Zymoseptoria tritici (or any other fungus) colonies grown at fixed inoculation positions on Petri dishes, alone (controls) or confronted with a bacterium inoculated in the centre.

Why colour and not grayscale

On a photographed plate the grey fungal colonies, the cream-white bacterial colony and its yellowish diffusion halo overlap strongly in grayscale brightness, so no single grey threshold can separate them. They are, however, well separated in the perceptually uniform CIELAB colour space: melanized hyphae are achromatic (chroma \(C^*_{ab}\) close to 0) and textured, whereas bacterial growth and the halo are warm (positive \(b^*\), hue angle ~60-100 degrees) and smooth. MycoHalo therefore

  1. converts sRGB to CIE 1976 \(L^*a^*b^*\) (D65),

  2. models the agar background and its illumination gradient (flat-field) with a robust polynomial surface,

  3. classifies every non-agar pixel as fungus, bacterium or halo with a Gaussian mixture initialised from the known plate layout, and

  4. separates individual colonies with a marker-controlled watershed seeded at the expected inoculation positions.

Main entry points

  • analyze_plate() — full pipeline for one image.

  • analyze_plates() — batch processing of a folder / file vector.

  • plot_qc() — quality-control overlay (always inspect!).

  • plot_melanization_map() — 3D shaded melanization landscape and 2D melanization map with the side-specific response.

  • plate_layout() — describe where colonies were inoculated.

  • simulate_plate() — synthetic plates with known ground truth, used for validation and unit tests.

  • compare_melanization() — plate-aware statistics.
